turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Thanks for coming in. I'll be direct. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so I had to give him a zero.
Okay. Let's look at the essay.
Which essay, and what does it show? Tell me what you're looking at and when you looked at it.
You're very sharp, you know that?
Don't manage me, Hale. Show me the essay and the date you gave him the zero.
No, really. You caught the timestamp issue in thirty seconds. That's sharp.
Don't manage me. Owen's zero is what we're here about. Tell me the date you entered it, and whether anyone called me before you did.
I just keep thinking, someone that sharp must see why I had to flag it.

"Why you had to flag it" is the question I'm asking you. A checker score is a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says not to use it alone. So what else do you have besides the 94 percent? Show me, and tell me the date you entered the zero.
